title: v14.2.x gives warning for `Invalid page configuration` for `middleware.ts`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: linear: turbopack
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Turbopack team.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/NakamotoInstitute/nakamotoinstitute.org

### To Reproduce

I do not know how to reproduce generally, so unfortunately my link is not a minimal reproduction but just a public repo I am experiencing this with.

This problem specifically occurs when I run `next dev --turbo`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior is I receive this message when loading any page. The page loads successfully despite this, but it creates a lot of uncertainty and confusion, as it only prints a blank replacement suggestion:

```
 ⚠ ./middleware.ts
Invalid page configuration
Page config in middleware.ts is deprecated. Replace `export const config=…` with the following:



 GET / 200 in 2426ms
```

Expected behavior is that middleware should be recognized as valid and work as it does without turbo.

```
 ✓ Compiled /middleware in 291ms (80 modules)
 ○ Compiling /[locale] ...
 ✓ Compiled /[locale] in 2.5s (678 modules)
 ✓ Compiled in 172ms (289 modules)
 GET / 200 in 2863ms
 ```

```bash

  Arch: x64

Next.js Config:

```


### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Middleware
Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

I tested with multiple 14.2.x releases with the same result. For now I am keeping my app on 14.1.x.
